mainEntity.name: How accurate is the U.S. Navy body fat formula?

acceptedAnswer.text: With careful measurements, the U.S. Navy body fat formula is commonly cited as landing within roughly 3 to 4 percentage points of DEXA for many people. It uses neck, waist, height, and, for women, hip circumference. Treat the result as an estimate and use repeated readings to track a trend.

mainEntity.name: What measurements do I need for this body fat calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need your height, neck circumference (measured just below the larynx), and waist circumference (measured at the narrowest point, typically at the navel). Women also need a hip circumference measurement at the widest point. You can use either imperial (inches) or metric (centimeters) units.

mainEntity.name: What is a healthy body fat percentage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Healthy body fat ranges vary by sex. For men: athletes 6–13%, fitness 14–17%, average 18–24%. For women: athletes 14–20%, fitness 21–24%, average 25–31%. Essential body fat — the minimum needed for organ function — is 2–5% for men and 10–13% for women.

mainEntity.name: How is body fat percentage different from BMI?

acceptedAnswer.text: BMI uses only height and weight, so it cannot distinguish between muscle and fat. A muscular person can have a high BMI but low body fat. Body fat percentage directly estimates the proportion of your body that is fat tissue, making it a much more useful metric for people who strength-train.
